$schema_note: Hand-verified game knowledge, NOT mechanically extracted from Hero_Siege.exe/data.win: these Controller_obj variable names are not present in Hero_Siege.exe (a static reading); the runtime fills the slots the code reads them through from data.win at run time, and no extractor currently produces them or ties them to Controller_obj, so they were found live, by content search. No generator produces this file or reads it; see docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md section '## 17. Stash Special Tabs & the Crafting Route' for the full write-up and ForgePact issue #14 (ForgePact/docs/crafting-materials-research.md) for the research.

materials.cell_path_note: the array being two-level is measured; the [x][y] axis order is from the static reading, not itself probed live

save.second_argument_note: as the close supplied it; its meaning is not measured

crafting_cube.note: whether the game's own count walks this grid is not observed; the grid's persistence across a save does not gate the build, per the owner's design (2026-09-24): only the craft's own items are placed here, at the press, and consumed at once

bag_to_stash_move.note: The routines the game's own Ctrl + left click runs to move one item from the bag into the stash tab on show, in that order, and the shapes that reproduced the move by name (ForgePact #68). Self and other are the two UI_Inventory_Grid_obj nodes told apart by uiNodeCallstack: InventoryGrid (the bag's, rebinding to the bag view on show) and StashGrid (the stash's, rebinding to the tab on show). The Socketable tab moved by hand only and has no by-name shape.

validate.arguments: the item struct; called again after the placement with self the StashGrid node
validate.answer: empty text, a refusal included (the Socketable tab's refusal of jewels shows nothing in it)

stack.arguments: the shown tab's cell array; 0 and 13 into the personal page, 9 and 2 into a shared page, the Materials tab and the Socketable tab; the item struct; the count to merge (1 on every hand move; the whole count merged by name); a small number (0 on a page and the Materials tab, 8 on the Socketable tab)
stack.answer: true after merging into a stack of the item's identity on that array; false when there is none, and then the grid placement follows

grid.arguments: the shown tab's cell array (the StashGrid node's nodeGrid on a page, Controller_obj.stashMaterialTab on the Materials tab), the item struct, 0, undefined
grid.answer: a struct of tabNumber, x, y, tabType, success; success=false when that array has no room, and no other tab is tried; tabNumber read 0 on shared page 1 too

source_clear.arguments: the item's anchor cell node in the bag grid's nodeGrid, read [y][x], then undefined; after a by-name placement (which leaves the item in its bag cells) or a merge, while the item is still on map 0 and before the owner step

owner_step.arguments: 0, 9, the item's key as text; only after a placement the re-read confirmed (alone, on an item still in the bag, it leaves the key on no map)

shared.map: not established: after the owner step the key answers on neither map 0 nor map 9 by GetItemFromFingerprint, as every shared-page key does

materials.owner_step: 0 to 9 for a new identity; none for a merge

socketable.owner_step: 0 to 9 for a new identity, by hand; none for a merge

cases: a class-10 item by hand and by name into the personal page and shared page 1, and against the full shared page 2
a new material identity by hand and by name into the Materials tab, one-unit and whole-stack (15) merges
a rune, a gem and an orb into the Socketable tab by hand; jewels and an Incarnation Gem refused by the game
one Materials-tab entry the bag stacks (Greater Unstable Dust, class 14, b=51)
one Socketable stack of 10 (Pristine Ruby, class 15, b=51)
